questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location — close to nature, easy to travel to my home country (Slovakia) by train.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy, I only had to search for the information about housing myself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a buddy that waited for my on the train station and walked with me to the dorm, helped to move in (also translated from German to English).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Various dorm buildings, but all managed by the same company, which is not the best (broken water pipes, no water for 4 days, unreasonable fire alarm outbursts,...).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: One shared kitchen for 18 people. One stove with 2 working plates. No shared pots nor plates...

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That their rights are very limited compared to their responsibilities. Management is slow in replying and any discomfort is compensated only by mail saying "sorry for the inconvenience".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Necessary to fill out several documents, but it was very similar to filing up the documentation for UCPH. To register into platforms for teaching, it was fairly straightforward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Course coordinator, coordinator of exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all classes I wanted to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Finding courses on the teaching platform to register for them can be tricky (Ilias). If you cannot find any course, try to text the responsible teacher or your course coordinator. Then you have to register for the exam, which is done on a separate platform (HohCampus).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses were somewhat general for MSc level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were somewhat general, they could go more in depth. Others were of what I expected and I had a lot of freedom to choose my own projects.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar, teachers share their presentations beforehand, which makes it easy to take notes. However, exams are written by hand on paper. I prefer UCPH style here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Weather and climate physics, Project in Landscape Ecology, Climate change, Mitigation and Adaptation (offered by UPCH), Global change issues.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: MSc thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Weather and climate physics — goes more into physics of climate, GHG, radiation, fundamental equations to understand movements of air, water and mass parcels.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There was a water pipe burst in our building not fixed for several days. I was traveling at the moment, but other students had to either move to a friend's place or to buy extra water (for drinking, basic hygiene, etc..) or to go to airbnb.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than what I expected. Housing was more — the area is notoriously known for high prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of sports available (dance, yoga, gymnastics, frisbee, football, martial arts...) were available on the campus for a small fee.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports activities. They are cheap and tutors are usually very good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore nature nearby, Wilhelma ZOO, Swabian Alps, Esslingen Am Neckar.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, but I had my own programme for the most of the time and met other international students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are pubs and parties happening multiple times a week on the campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not speaking the language naturally leads to being excluded from the locals that already formed their cliques — not dissimilar to anywhere else.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Equal rights to everybody.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Living on campus means everything is close by (lectures, sport activities, parties, dinning hall), but you will be somewhat excluded from the city. 
Some teachers do not respond immediately, and you need to send them a reminder, or even knock on their door. Sometimes just reach another person instead. 
This area is very close and well connected to other countries in Europe by trains and buses (France, Austria, Switzerland, other regions of Germany). I suggest to use this opportunity.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Food is cheaper than in DK, even cheaper than in some other countries in EU. Eating outside is can be comparable or a bit cheaper.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing the country's nature and meeting some of my best friends there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not responding teachers. I still struggle to get my grades from 3 months ago.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was amazing to have the option to go and travel :) Thank you for the support.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
